subject: Information Theory
title: Why the Log?
description: A quick, practical guide to Why the Log?.

hook.text: Why does Shannon's formula use a logarithm? Not for elegance—for a very practical reason.

buildup.text: Logarithms make information additive. Two independent coin flips carry 2 bits, not 4.

discovery.text: Without the log, combining sources would multiply their information. Addition is far more natural.

twist.text: The log also compresses the scale. An event with probability one in a billion gives only about 30 bits.

climax.text: The base of the log picks the unit: base 2 gives bits, base e gives nats, base 10 gives hartleys.

punchline.text: The log makes surprises add up neatly.

quiz.question: Why does Shannon's entropy formula use a logarithm?
options: To make the formula look complex
To make information from independent events additive
